record_type_quote: As part of the Systematizing Confidence in Open Research and Evidence (SCORE) program, the present study consisted of a two-stage replication test of a central finding by Pennycook et al. (2020), namely that asking people to think about the accuracy of a single headline improves “truth discernment” of intentions to share news headlines about COVID-19.

targets.authors: Pennycook G., McPhetres J., Zhang Y., Lu J. G., Rand D. G.
targets.title: Fighting COVID-19 misinformation on social media: Experimental evidence for a scalable accuracy-nudge intervention
targets.evidence_quote:
The focal hypothesis that we replicated in this study was determined through SCORE and stemmed from Study 2 of
Pennycook et al. (2020)
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly describe partial agreement overall; stage-one failure, pooled effect, and differing true/false-headline pattern. Study 1 accuracy condition also partially replicated as described in footnote 6.

reasoning: Identity checked against title and all three authors. Complete article including reference list acquired via Europe PMC XML. Only Pennycook et al. 2020 is a target; subsequent Pennycook 2021 work is contextual.
